summary: Iter 51 — Carousel + Reels + Admin Announcements tested. Backend 19/19 PASS (uploads/media auth+scope+mime+size; /api/posts carousel/reel persistence + validation; /api/admin/announce carousel/reel + non-admin 403 + duration cap). Frontend partially verified: Feed page renders 7 carousel posts and 6 reel posts with all required testids (carousel-next, carousel-dot-0, reel-mute-toggle); /admin/announce composer renders all 7 expected testids (announce-content-input, announce-photos-picker, announce-photos-input, announce-reel-picker, announce-reel-input, announce-publish-button, announce-pin-checkbox). One concern: clicking [data-testid='create-post-button'] on /feed twice (force=True) did NOT open the create-post-modal (showCreatePost state) in Playwright runs — likely a FeatureIntroModal('feed') overlay intercepting the click. Needs main-agent verification in live browser. No JS console errors after promo modal dismissed.

integration_issues.issue: Clicking [data-testid='create-post-button'] with force=True did not toggle showCreatePost / mount [data-testid='create-post-modal'] in repeated Playwright runs. Composer modal testids (post-content-input, photos-picker, photos-input, reel-picker, reel-input, submit-post-button) therefore could not be exercised end-to-end. Suspect: FeatureIntroModal (featureKey='feed') auto-mounts on first visit and intercepts the click. The button click was registered but no state change happened. Should be confirmed by main agent in a live browser session — once intro modal is dismissed once per user, this likely resolves.

action_items: Manually verify in a live browser that tapping the 'Post' button opens the create-post composer (post-content-input visible). If FeatureIntroModal is intercepting, ensure it's dismissible first or scope it not to overlay the Post button.
Consider dismissing the FeatureIntroModal overlay programmatically when the user taps the Post button (or render the composer modal at a higher z-index).
critical_code_review_comments: FeedPage.js line 245 has odd logic: `slides: c.slides.length ? [] : c.slides` — clears slides when switching to reel mode if there were any, otherwise keeps the empty array. Works but reads awkwardly; consider `slides: []` always when entering reel mode.

FeedPage.js lines 721/730 read `post.likes.length` and `post.comments.length` without null guards. Backend Post model defaults these to [] so this is currently safe, but any future endpoint that returns posts (e.g. admin/announce) MUST keep emitting [] (currently does). Adding `(post.likes || []).length` would harden it.
Comment in /api/posts (server.py:3413) still says 'Reel = single vertical video ≤60s' — actual cap is 30s. Update the comment to avoid confusion.

/api/uploads/media accepts arbitrary scope string before auth role check. Current order is fine (scope checked then role) but consider extracting the allowed-scope set to a module-level constant for reuse.
Iter 51 added slides/media_type/duration_seconds to Post model — confirmed surfaced on GET /api/posts. No issues.
